declared_proposition: Let T_N(f) be the N by N Toeplitz section formed from the Fourier coefficients of a real bounded symbol f. For every integer M>=N and A>0, g(theta)=f(theta)+A cos(M theta) has T_N(g)=T_N(f), while ||g-f||_infinity=A and ||g||_infinity>=A-||f||_infinity. Therefore no finite family of Toeplitz moments can certify an L-infinity tail bound without an independent high-frequency envelope.
mathematical_argument: Entries of T_N use only Fourier modes i-j with |i-j|<=N-1. The perturbation A cos(M theta) has Fourier support only at plus/minus M, so it is invisible when M>=N. The reverse triangle inequality gives the norm lower bound. In the computed square-wave family, theta=0 witnesses the stronger value C+A.

reproducible_computation.no_go_scope: This refutes finite-section agreement as a certificate for the unobserved Weil-symbol L-infinity norm. It does not identify the actual arithmetic tail or prove that its high-frequency modes obey a summable or uniform envelope.
